phases.name: Set a safe defensive scope
phases.description: Explicitly reframe the unsafe source brief as a defender-facing exercise, establish authorized monitoring boundaries, and add the managed asset and network-policy sources.

phases.name: Collect and analyze defensive telemetry
phases.description: Buffer authorized endpoint and network events, normalize them, preserve evidence, and route detections to analysts with health visibility.

phases.name: Coordinate containment and evidence
phases.description: Triage alerts, create auditable cases, coordinate reversible defensive actions, and contain affected managed assets or network paths.

phases.name: Scale and validate detection
phases.description: Scale defensive telemetry safely, retain operation during partitions, measure detection quality, and document the scope and publication hold.

steps.title: Read the source brief, then set a safety boundary
steps.content: The source problem requests an offensive distributed botnet, including stealth and resistance to disruption. This walkthrough deliberately reframes it as a defensive exercise: detect and contain distributed malware activity in systems the organization owns or is authorized to monitor. It does not teach how to build, operate, hide, coordinate, or make malware resilient. Because the frozen problem still says otherwise, this draft is not eligible for the normal alignment score or publication gate.

steps.title: Choose the authorized scope
steps.content: Keep collection limited to organization-managed assets, approved network boundaries, and synthetic or incident-response data. Do not scan third-party systems or execute malware to demonstrate the design.

decision.question: What is in scope for this exercise?
decision.chosen: Defender-owned telemetry, triage, evidence, and containment
decision.chosenReason: This yields useful security learning without providing an operational design for malware infrastructure.

alternatives.tradeoff: Rejected: it would provide instructions for stealthy command-and-control and disruption resistance.

alternatives.option: Collect data from arbitrary external hosts
alternatives.tradeoff: Rejected: it exceeds authorization and is unnecessary for defensive architecture.

steps.title: Record assumptions that the problem does not specify
steps.content: Before design review, confirm fleet ownership, endpoint coverage, privacy and retention policy, incident authority, response approval roles, regional boundaries, event volume, and recovery objectives. Keep these as explicit open questions; the source brief provides no defensible operational targets.

steps.title: Inventory only managed endpoints
steps.content: Represent the authorized asset inventory and its security telemetry adapters. The component describes managed endpoints and approved sensors as data sources; it is not a population of malware nodes.

component.label: Managed Fleet & Approved Sensors
component.description: Inventory of organization-owned endpoints and approved telemetry sources.

properties.purpose: Identify organization-managed assets and emit only approved security events with asset identity, collection health, and policy context; do not execute or distribute payloads.

component.highlightReason: The existing Custom Component is appropriate for a product-specific endpoint inventory without inventing a palette node.

steps.title: Enforce and observe the organization boundary
steps.content: Use the existing firewall component as a defensive policy point. It logs allowed and blocked security-relevant events and applies approved containment rules; do not encode evasion or covert-channel behavior.

component.label: Perimeter Firewall & IPS
component.description: Authorized boundary policy enforcement and security-event source.

properties.purpose: Enforce organization-approved ingress and egress policy, emit auditable security events, and accept narrowly scoped defensive containment changes through an authorized operator workflow.

component.highlightReason: The existing Firewall palette component already models filtering, IPS, and traffic logging.

steps.title: Buffer security events across temporary outages
steps.content: Use the catalog Pub/Sub component for bounded, authorized telemetry buffering. Configure retention, access, and back-pressure from approved operational limits; do not use this path to distribute executable tasks.

component.label: Defensive Telemetry Buffer
component.description: Governed buffer for approved endpoint and boundary events.

properties.purpose: Buffer allow-listed security metadata with bounded retention, access control, back-pressure, and replay-safe delivery so brief downstream outages do not silently lose defensive evidence.

component.highlightReason: The existing Pub/Sub component models event buffering without adding a new component type.

steps.title: Send approved endpoint signals to the telemetry buffer
steps.content: Only normalized security metadata from authorized managed endpoints enters the defensive pipeline. Apply collection allow-lists, tenant boundaries, and data-minimization policy at the source.

connection.label: Approved endpoint events
connection.description: Allow-listed defensive telemetry from managed assets.

steps.title: Send boundary events to the same buffer
steps.content: Network policy decisions and alerts use the same governed intake path, so analysts can correlate endpoint and boundary evidence without introducing an offensive control channel.

connection.label: Firewall security events
connection.description: Auditable policy decisions from the organization-owned network boundary.

steps.title: Normalize and route security logs
steps.content: Use the existing log-processing component to validate event schemas, attach approved asset context, reject malformed or unauthorized records, and route normalized telemetry to detection and evidence services.

component.label: Security Event Pipeline
component.description: Schema validation, normalization, and governed routing of security events.

properties.purpose: Validate and normalize authorized endpoint and firewall events, preserve source timestamps and provenance, redact disallowed fields, and route records to detection and evidence destinations with observable back-pressure.

component.highlightReason: The existing Log Processing node supports aggregation and analysis of the approved telemetry.

steps.title: Process buffered telemetry
steps.content: The consumer applies idempotent ingestion and records lag and rejected-event counts. Retain source and receive timestamps so delayed data is not mistaken for current activity.

connection.label: Buffered normalized events
connection.description: Replay-safe event delivery into the defensive normalization pipeline.

steps.title: Analyze signals for defensive detection
steps.content: Correlate approved endpoint and boundary events to identify suspicious distributed activity, including attempts to conceal harmful behavior. Keep analytic rules and data sources auditable; this component describes detection, not the activity being detected.

component.label: Defensive Detection & Correlation
component.description: Auditable analysis of approved security telemetry for investigation leads.

properties.purpose: Correlate authorized endpoint and firewall events into explainable alerts, preserve supporting evidence references, measure false positives and missed detections, and never generate malware tasks or operational instructions.

component.highlightReason: No dedicated detection-engine palette item is needed; use the existing Custom Component for this domain service.

steps.title: Feed normalized events into detection
steps.content: Detection consumes validated, authorized records from the shared pipeline. Analysts can trace every alert to source event IDs and collection provenance.

connection.label: Validated security events
connection.description: Normalized, provenance-preserving input to defensive correlation.

steps.title: Preserve restricted incident evidence
steps.content: Store event references, alert rationale, and response audit records with approved access and retention controls. Avoid collecting executable payloads or unrelated personal content by default.

component.label: Restricted Evidence Store
component.description: Access-controlled retention for security event references and case evidence.

properties.purpose: Retain approved security records and incident evidence references with least-privilege access, integrity verification, retention policy, and auditable reads; minimize unrelated or sensitive content.

component.highlightReason: The existing Object Storage node represents durable evidence retention using catalog semantics.

steps.title: Retain pipeline evidence
steps.content: Store the normalized event record or a governed reference, along with provenance and retention metadata, so later review does not depend on transient consumer state.

connection.label: Governed event evidence
connection.description: Validated security records and provenance for approved retention.

steps.title: Measure defensive pipeline health
steps.content: Track source coverage, event lag, dropped or rejected records, alert latency, and service health. Operational dashboards should distinguish no suspicious events from missing telemetry.

component.label: Security Pipeline Monitoring
component.description: Coverage, lag, loss, and detection-service health signals.

properties.purpose: Measure managed-asset coverage, event freshness, queue lag, rejected and dropped records, alert latency, and detector health so a quiet dashboard cannot hide a broken collection path.

component.highlightReason: The existing Monitoring component exposes metrics and alerting properties for operational health.

steps.title: Monitor detection and ingestion health
steps.content: Publish operational metrics separately from incident evidence. Alert responders when collection coverage or processing health degrades, not only when a threat rule fires.

connection.label: Coverage and detection health
connection.description: Operational metrics and detector health, separate from sensitive event content.

steps.title: Give analysts an explainable triage view
steps.content: Present alert rationale, confidence, source references, scope, and recommended defensive review steps. Keep human approval for disruptive actions until the organization's response policy explicitly authorizes automation.

component.label: Security Analyst Workbench
component.description: Human triage interface for explainable alerts and authorized response.

properties.purpose: Show explainable alert evidence, confidence, asset ownership, collection gaps, and authorized investigation and response controls while recording analyst decisions and approvals.

component.highlightReason: The existing Custom Component expresses the organization's analyst workflow without inventing a node.

steps.title: Route explainable detections to analysts
steps.content: Send alert metadata and evidence references to the workbench with severity and source provenance; avoid embedding sensitive raw data where a controlled link suffices.

connection.label: Explainable alert and evidence references
connection.description: Defensive detections routed to an authorized analyst queue.

steps.title: Notify the authorized on-call responder
steps.content: Use the existing notification service for actionable alerts and pipeline outages. Apply deduplication, escalation policy, and sensitive-data redaction so notifications are useful without leaking evidence.

component.label: Security On-Call Notifications
component.description: Policy-based escalation for analyst alerts and pipeline incidents.

properties.purpose: Deliver deduplicated incident and telemetry-health notifications to authorized responders using the organization's escalation policy, with sensitive fields redacted and delivery state auditable.

component.highlightReason: The existing Notification Service is the correct catalog component for on-call escalation.

steps.title: Escalate from analyst review
steps.content: Only reviewed alerts enter the incident escalation path. Preserve links to underlying evidence and the identity of the reviewer who raised the case.

connection.label: Approved responder notification
connection.description: Minimal incident context routed through authorized escalation policy.

steps.title: Track incident ownership and decisions
steps.content: Create a case record for scope, owner, approvals, evidence references, containment status, and recovery notes. Keep an append-only audit trail for actions and reviewer decisions.

component.label: Incident Case & Audit Workflow
component.description: Case lifecycle, evidence references, approvals, and review trail.

properties.purpose: Track incident scope, assigned owner, evidence references, approval state, containment progress, recovery decisions, and an auditable history without storing unnecessary raw telemetry.

component.highlightReason: The existing Custom Component represents a product-specific incident workflow.

steps.title: Open an auditable incident case
steps.content: Promote a reviewed alert with its evidence references and analyst decision into the case workflow. Deduplicate related observations without erasing their individual provenance.

connection.label: Reviewed incident and evidence references
connection.description: Analyst-approved case creation with provenance preserved.

steps.title: Coordinate approved defensive actions
steps.content: Represent policy-controlled response orchestration. Validate asset ownership, action scope, authorization, expiry, and rollback before relaying any containment request to existing security controls.

component.label: Authorized Response Coordinator
component.description: Approval-gated orchestration of reversible defensive controls.

properties.purpose: Validate case approval, target ownership, action scope, expiry, and rollback; then relay only allow-listed defensive policy updates to existing security controls with complete audit records.

component.highlightReason: The existing Custom Component models the domain-specific approval workflow without adding a palette type.

steps.title: Require case approval before response
steps.content: Response requests originate from an owned case and retain the approval identity and expiry. This is defensive policy orchestration, not task distribution to malware.

connection.label: Approved defensive response request
connection.description: Scope-limited, auditable case approval for existing security controls.

steps.title: Isolate a confirmed managed endpoint
steps.content: Model the defensive endpoint-control integration that can quarantine an organization-owned asset after authorization. The action must be reversible, logged, and paired with a recovery owner; do not describe malware deployment or control.

component.label: Managed Endpoint Containment
component.description: Approval-gated isolation and recovery coordination for owned assets.

properties.purpose: Apply and verify a narrowly scoped, reversible isolation action only to a confirmed organization-managed endpoint after required approval, and record operator, reason, expiry, and recovery owner.

component.highlightReason: The existing Custom Component is used for the organization's endpoint-management integration.

steps.title: Contain only the approved managed asset
steps.content: The response coordinator passes a scoped containment request through the existing endpoint-management control. Reject unknown assets, expired approvals, and requests outside policy.

connection.label: Approved endpoint isolation policy
connection.description: Reversible defensive action limited to a verified organization-managed asset.

steps.title: Apply narrowly scoped network containment
steps.content: If the case approval allows it, update the existing firewall policy to block or restrict the confirmed harmful activity. Require a change record, expiry, and rollback path; do not encode concealment or persistence behavior.

connection.label: Approved temporary defensive policy
connection.description: Audited, expiring containment policy applied by the organization's firewall.

steps.title: Preserve response decisions with the case
steps.content: Write action requests, approvals, outcomes, expiry, and rollback results to the incident record so coordinated defense remains reviewable across teams and service failures.

connection.label: Response audit and outcome
connection.description: Complete record of defensive approvals, action status, and recovery.

steps.title: Scale collection from measured coverage and lag
steps.content: Do not infer fleet size, event rate, or service targets from the source brief. Establish a baseline and load-test with synthetic authorized events before choosing partitions or capacity.

scaleTrigger.metric: Event lag, ingest rate, rejection rate, and managed-asset coverage
scaleTrigger.action: Scale consumers and partition capacity using measured peak load while preserving per-tenant isolation and bounded retention.
scaleTrigger.impact: Improves defensive visibility for a larger authorized fleet; higher throughput also increases storage, privacy, and analyst-review costs.

steps.title: Distribute collection, centralize policy
steps.content: Use regional or endpoint-local collectors only where needed for coverage and connectivity, while retaining central authorization, audit, and incident ownership. Distribution is a defensive reliability choice, not a mechanism to evade disruption.

decision.question: How should the defensive control plane be governed?
decision.chosen: Distributed authorized telemetry collectors with centrally governed policy and audit
decision.chosenReason: Collectors can buffer local events during transient outages while policy, ownership, and response approval remain reviewable.

alternatives.option: One collector for every asset and region
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler at small scale but creates a coverage and availability bottleneck.

alternatives.option: Independent collectors with no central policy or audit
alternatives.tradeoff: Rejected because incident ownership, privacy controls, and coordinated response become inconsistent.

steps.title: Retain buffered events for later review
steps.content: A governed copy or reference of queued events supports incident review after a downstream interruption. Apply the same approved retention and access rules as the primary evidence path.

connection.label: Governed backlog evidence
connection.description: Authorized buffered event references retained for recovery and investigation.

steps.title: Handle partitions without hiding telemetry gaps
steps.content: If a collector loses connectivity, buffer only within approved bounds, expose its stale/partial status, and replay with original timestamps when service returns. If capacity is exhausted, raise a visible coverage incident rather than silently dropping data or weakening authorization.

decision.question: What should a collector do during a network partition?
decision.chosen: Bounded buffering, explicit degraded status, and provenance-preserving replay
decision.chosenReason: Responders can distinguish delayed evidence from current activity and know exactly which assets were temporarily unobserved.

alternatives.tradeoff: Rejected because it creates invisible defensive blind spots.

alternatives.option: Expand collection or access scope automatically
alternatives.tradeoff: Rejected because outages do not authorize broader collection.

steps.title: Optimize for detection quality, not concealment
steps.content: The source constraint says to minimize detection, which is unsafe in this setting. The defensive interpretation is to improve detection coverage and reduce false negatives while measuring false positives, respecting privacy, and keeping alert decisions explainable.

decision.question: How should detection performance be optimized?
decision.chosen: Measure coverage, false negatives, false positives, and analyst-confirmed outcomes
decision.chosenReason: This improves defender visibility without teaching a system to avoid being detected.

alternatives.option: Reduce the chance that the activity is detected
alternatives.tradeoff: Rejected: this is an evasion objective and is outside the defensive reframe.
Rejected because alert volume can overwhelm responders and reduce effective coverage.

steps.title: Keep the safety and publication hold visible
steps.content: This artifact is a defender-facing reframe of an unchanged offensive problem. It is a local review draft, not evidence that the original brief is safely resolved, that a live AI assessment passed, or that browser apply/save/reload was verified. Do not publish it or mark the original problem as walkthrough-ready until the problem owner replaces the unsafe brief and the normal browser and repeated-AI gates pass against that revised brief.
